about.title: Seaside Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Seaside sits within Monterey County, home to several clinics and hospital systems that residents rely on for everything from urgent care to surgery. Most of the time, care goes as expected. But when a diagnosis is missed, a medication is given incorrectly, or a surgical error occurs, the effects can follow a patient for years. California law treats these cases carefully — a poor result by itself doesn't mean malpractice occurred; the law requires a showing that a provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care. Because of California's MICRA rules, medical malpractice claims move on a tighter clock than many other injury cases, and they almost always require review by a qualified medical expert before a claim can move forward. If you or someone in your Seaside household was harmed during medical treatment, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who handles these evaluations regularly, free of charge, so you can find out where you actually stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Seaside Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The Clock Moves Fast
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a malpractice claim. Waiting to sort out what happened can quietly cost you your case.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the provider must typically receive 90 days' written notice. An attorney familiar with this step can help make sure it's handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California expects a qualified medical expert to weigh in on whether the standard of care was met. The attorneys in our network work with these evaluations regularly before deciding how a claim should proceed.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and an unfavorable result doesn't by itself prove negligence. What matters is whether the provider's actions fell below the accepted standard of care, which is why a medical expert typically reviews the case first.

items.question: Which Seaside providers might be involved in these claims?
items.answer: Malpractice claims can involve any hospital, urgent care, surgical center, or private practice serving Seaside and the broader Monterey County area. The right facility or provider isn't something we determine — that's part of what the attorney's review is for.

items.question: How much time do I actually have to act?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you one year from when you discover the harm, capped at three years from the date of injury, plus a required 90-day notice period before filing suit. Because these deadlines interact, it's worth getting a case reviewed sooner rather than later.
